items.name: WinMinmax Sliding-Window Min/Max Tracker
items.symbol: minmax_running_min(), minmax_running_max(), minmax_subwin_update(), struct minmax { s[3] }, struct minmax_sample { t, v }
items.counter_case: EWMA already drives compaction decisions adequately. WinMinmax adds value only if Cortex needs to distinguish 'worst case in window' from 'average over window' — useful for dashboards but not strictly required for operational decisions.

items.name: LruCache max_pending_changes Back-pressure Gate
items.symbol: lc->max_pending_changes, lc->pending_changes, lc->to_be_changed, LC_STARVING flag, lc_is_used(), lc_get() returns NULL when starving
items.counter_case: A starving back-pressure gate would stall interactive MCP tool calls (save_concept) when the dirty queue is full. Apply only to background ingest path; never gate user-triggered saves.

items.name: errseq Error-Subscription Sampling
items.symbol: errseq_set(), errseq_sample(), errseq_check(), errseq_check_and_advance(), ERRSEQ_SEEN bit, ERRSEQ_CTR_INC, ERRSEQ_SHIFT
items.counter_case: Node.js is single-threaded; a thrown exception from an awaited write already propagates. errseq is most valuable for fire-and-forget writes where the caller does not await the result — apply only to those paths.

items.name: io_alloc_cache Fixed-Size Object Pool
items.symbol: IO_ALLOC_CACHE_MAX=128, io_alloc_cache_put(), io_alloc_cache_get(), io_cache_alloc(), io_cache_free(), struct io_alloc_cache { entries, nr_cached, max_cached, elem_size, init_clear }
items.counter_case: Node.js GC handles short-lived objects well; manual object pooling only beats GC if allocation is measurably hot in a profile. Apply only after profiling shows allocation overhead in cortex_find or build_context_pack hot path.

items.name: TimerQueue rb_root_cached O(1) Next-Expiry
items.symbol: timerqueue_add(), timerqueue_del(), timerqueue_iterate_next(), rb_add_cached(), rb_root_cached.rb_leftmost, struct timerqueue_head, struct timerqueue_node { expires }
items.counter_case: At <5000 entities, O(n) tick scan completes in <1ms and requires no parallel data structure. TimerQueue only matters at high entity counts or high tick frequency. Profile before implementing.

items.name: IntervalTree Line-Range Entity Lookup
items.symbol: INTERVAL_TREE_DEFINE macro, interval_tree_insert(), interval_tree_remove(), interval_tree_iter_first(), interval_tree_iter_next(), __subtree_last augmentation
items.counter_case: At <5000 entities, a linear scan for overlapping intervals is <1ms. Interval tree only pays off on large repos with frequent impact_analysis calls. Profile first; the augmented rb-tree adds implementation complexity.

items.name: list_sort Bottom-Up Iterative Merge Sort
items.violated_principle: JavaScript Array.prototype.sort() is stable (ES2019+) and handles all Cortex sort needs. Custom linked-list merge sort adds complexity with no measurable benefit at Cortex's entity counts.

items.name: percpu-refcount Two-Phase Refcount
items.violated_principle: Designed for multi-CPU systems to avoid cache-line contention. Node.js is single-threaded; per-CPU splitting adds allocation overhead and two-phase shutdown complexity with no benefit.

items.name: io-wq Bounded Kernel Thread Pool
items.symbol: WORKER_IDLE_TIMEOUT=5*HZ, WORKER_INIT_LIMIT=3, struct io_wq_acct { max_workers, nr_workers, nr_running }, io_wq_create(), io_wq_enqueue()
items.violated_principle: Manages kernel threads with CPU affinity and idle timeout. Node.js is event-loop based with no worker threads in Cortex's hot path. Thread pool management is irrelevant.

items.name: Missing Async Re-entrancy Assert on Mutating Cache Methods
items.pattern: Cortex's ExperienceManager has no re-entrancy guard. An await inside maybeCompact() allows a second call to enter before the first exits, causing double-compaction or corrupt LRU state. The LC_PARANOIA pattern detects this at runtime with a single atomic bit.
items.proposed_action: Add a '_busy: boolean' flag to ExperienceManager; throw/warn on re-entry in maybeCompact(), evict(), flush(). CLAUDE.md rule: all async mutating methods on ExperienceManager must assert !_busy at entry and reset in finally.
